{{TabbedHeader|tab1=Status Effects|tab2=Enemy-Exclusive Effects|tab2name=Enemy-Exclusive Status Effects}}
'''Status Effects''' are conditions that can be applied to units on either side of a battle through the use of Passives, Skills, E.G.O Gifts and even other status effects.

__TOC__

== Overview ==

A status effect can use up to two values to function, which will be called 'modes' here for clarity:
* Zero-value mode, where the value is always fixed at 1 and has no inherent effect on the status effect's strength.
* Single-value mode, where the value is typically called '''Count''', '''Stack''' or simply '''Value'''.
* Double-value mode, where one value is called '''Potency''' and the other '''Count'''. Generally, Potency determines the strength of the effect, while Count determines its duration.

In single-value or double-value modes, if one or more of the values reach 0, the status effect is removed from the unit. Additionally, the values of a status effect are always consumed before they are gained or inflicted.

If the status effect uses both values, the Potency will be displayed on the bottom left, with the Count on the bottom right. Otherwise, the value is always displayed on the bottom left.

Status effects also come with a few attributes:
* '''Base Value''', the initial value of the status effect upon infliction if no value is specified.
* '''Max Value''', the maximum value of the status effect. The default Max Value is 99.

Status effects are also separated into three categories:
* Positive status effects, which are highlighted in <font color="#fac400"><u>yellow</u></font>.
* Neutral status effects, which are highlighted in <font color="#9f6a3a"><u>brown</u></font>.
* Negative status effects, which are highlighted in <font color="#e20000"><u>red</u></font>.
Note that a status being classified as positive or negative does not necessarily mean its effects are fully beneficial or detrimental. From the gameplay perspective, this classification primarily matters for the purposes of effects such as "Deal +10% damage for every negative status effect on this unit".

<!--To those adding new Status Effects to the page: faction/abnormality exclusive effects have to show signs of really belonging to that faction for it to count. For example, although Rupture Protection is currently exclusive to Molar Boatworks identities, there is no evidence that it will stay like that in the future. On the other hand, Charge Barrier really has W Corp.'s style to it, and therefore would likely stay exclusive to W Corp. identities in the future, so it is listed as such.-->

== Buffs ==
Positive Status Effects (or Buffs) provide beneficial effects to the receiver.

==Neutral Effects==
Neutral Status Effects either have both positive and negative effects, or have no significant effect on the user. <br> Some Neutral Status Effects are used as expendable resources, with Skills being enhanced or cancelled due to the Value of these Effects.

==Trivia==
* ''Limbus Company'' uses two different sets of descriptions for status effects: one for when it is viewed in the descriptions of Skills and Passives, and one for when it is inflicted onto and listed under a unit.
** While most status effects only possess minor discrepancies between these two, some can have significant differences, such as {{StatusEffect|Weak-resist DMG Boost}}, which lists the damage increase as "10% per Count" on the first and "1% per Count" on the latter. The status effect itself functions based on the "1% per Count" basis.
*** This discrepancy likely caused confusion among the developers of the game as well, as the [[Peccatulum Irae Class 2]] only gained 1 {{StatusEffect|Weak-resist DMG Boost}} from its Skills, likely due to the assumption that this would result in a 10% damage increase when it is only 1% in reality. This was likely caused by the fact that {{StatusEffect|Weak-resist DMG Boost}} did not appear as part of any Skill or Passive description, thus never requiring the first set.
